paragraphs: Before opening, cooks thaw and prepare ingredients and set up stations. During slower mornings, they fill orders as received. Lunch and dinner rushes bring continuous frying and assembly, with kitchen and front-counter teams coordinating pace. Before closing, cooks clean stations, verify sanitation and temperatures, record waste and inventory, and prepare for the next day.

In one sentence: turn ingredients into standardized meals quickly. Duties include preparation, frying, assembly, pace control, sanitation, and training. The work is repetitive but demands speed and consistency.
